title: Contextual Alpha Labs: interactive snippet deck for first-time console flows
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: New developer users land in the Console with feature-dense surfaces (dashboards, rollouts, cost charts) and often drop off before completing a workable integration. Goal: ship a lightweight, contextual interactive 'Alpha Labs' snippet deck that surfaces 3 guided microflows (Create first request, Visualize cost for sample workload, Configure rollout with canary) inside empty or low-activity console states. The deck must be composable (snippets can be shown inline or expanded into a sandbox), respect team RBAC, and gracefully collapse once a user completes any microflow. This ticket covers research synthesis, low-fi wireframes, an interactive Figma prototype, and two short moderated usability sessions. Constraints: should avoid adding global modals, must work within current console chrome, and support i18n-ready copy. Success metric: 10% lift in new workspace activation within 14 days and 80% task completion in moderated tests.
acceptance_criteria: Three distinct microflows implemented as design artifacts: Request Quickstart, Cost Snapshot, Canary Rollout Wizard
Figma interactive prototype with branching states for success, skip, and collapse
Usability test report with N=8 participants and prioritized list of fixes
Hand-off package (tokens, spacing, copy variants, accessibility notes) uploaded to Drive and synced with dev engineer
